title: The water cycle
subject: Science
objectives: Name the four main stages of the water cycle.
Explain how heat from the sun drives evaporation.
Give an everyday example of condensation.

blocks.text: The water on Earth is always moving. It goes from rivers and seas into the air, falls back as rain or snow, and flows back to the sea. This never-ending journey is called the water cycle.

blocks.alt: A diagram of the sun, the sea, clouds, rain on mountains and a river flowing back to the sea
blocks.caption: The water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.

blocks.text: The sun heats water in seas, lakes and rivers. Some of the water turns into an invisible gas called water vapour and rises into the air. This change from liquid to gas is evaporation.

blocks.definition: Water in the form of a gas. We cannot see it.

blocks.title: Drying clothes
blocks.text: Wet clothes on a line become dry on a sunny day because the water in them evaporates into the air.
High in the sky the air is colder. Water vapour cools and turns back into tiny drops of liquid water. Millions of these drops together make clouds.

blocks.title: A cold glass
blocks.text: Drops form on the outside of a glass of cold water because water vapour in the room cools on the glass and condenses.
When the drops in a cloud join and become too heavy, they fall as rain, snow, sleet or hail. This is precipitation.

items: Some water flows over the land into streams and rivers.
Some soaks into the ground and becomes groundwater.
Rivers carry the water back to lakes and the sea, where the cycle starts again.
Evaporation: the sun heats water and it rises as vapour.
Condensation: the vapour cools and forms clouds.
Precipitation: water falls as rain or snow.
Collection: water gathers in rivers, lakes, seas and the ground.

questions.prompt: What gives water the energy to evaporate?
questions.explanation: The sun heats the water, and the heat turns some of it into water vapour.
Water vapour cools and condenses into tiny drops, which we see as clouds.

questions.prompt: Hail is a kind of precipitation.
questions.explanation: Rain, snow, sleet and hail are all precipitation.

questions.prompt: What is the change from water vapour to liquid water called?
questions.explanation: Cooling turns the gas back into a liquid: that is condensation.

questions.prompt: Evaporation only happens at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Water evaporates slowly at any temperature; heat makes it faster. 100 degrees is where it boils.

terms.definition: Liquid water turning into water vapour.
Water vapour cooling and turning back into liquid water.
Water falling from clouds as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
Water that soaks into the ground and is stored under the surface.

summary: The sun heats water, which evaporates into water vapour. The vapour cools and condenses into clouds. Water falls as precipitation and collects in rivers, lakes, seas and the ground, and the cycle starts again.
